Hypothesis of the change: Building on c013 (score +0.619, decay<=0.5, max_net_weight<=8), raise the finite weight cap modestly from 8 to 11.2 (x1.4) so that the most critical nets get slightly more pull without returning to the uncapped regime that hurt TNS spreading — a conservative refinement that should preserve the TNS gains while nudging WNS.

If some runs are INVALID (failures listed), first say what kind of failure it is (legality / crash / timeout) and whether it looks systematic (all seeds of a case) or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which case/metric moved and plausible mechanism, (3) one concrete next-step suggestion. No preamble.

response: The hypothesis held: raising the cap 8→11.2 preserved TNS gains while improving WNS across all three cases (all valid, no failures). WNS rose +3.9% (ariane), +14.1% (bp), +22.3% (bp_fe); TNS also improved (+1.4%, +21.5%, +17.5%), so the conservative cap avoided the uncapped regime's TNS-spreading penalty. Mechanism: critical nets get slightly more pull, tightening WNS without over-constraining routing/overflow. Next step: sweep cap 9.6–12.8 to locate the WNS/TNS optimum before committing.
